function.name: light_travel_time
function.description: Calculate the time taken for light to travel from a celestial body to another. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

The function probably returns time in seconds or maybe in years. We need to decide. The function name suggests it calculates time. Usually you'd convert distance in light years to meters: 1 ly = c * 1 year. So time = distance / speed_of_light? Actually if distance is given in light years, then time in years is just distance. But if we want seconds, we need to multiply by seconds per year. But the function might do that. Let's assume it returns time in seconds. We'll call it.
